title: Verify GetSeatMap sets getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID and Book consumes them as ResponseId/selectedOfferId when SeatMap precedes it
request_summary: Book (GulfAir/KSA, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01, 1 ADT, no seat) with ResponseId/selectedOfferId taken straight from the GetSeatMap response
response_summary: 200 - pnr QRDHHX, bookingToken TPC60517146494D2992026, gdsPNR "", ticket 722136995952
expected: GetSeatMap returns 200 with non-empty offerId/responseId; Book accepts them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without AddPassenger's IDs being re-sent
actual: Confirmed. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (identical to the AddPassenger values); Book accepted them and created a real PNR. The Postman collection-variable assignment itself (getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID) is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP - verified the field mapping it relies on (resp.offerId/resp.responseId) instead. Unchanged from Rounds 1-7.
evidence: GetSeatMap resp.responseId a9258155-8fee-4561-9dfa-d56526bf84dd == AddPassenger responseId; Book echoed as request ResponseId; pnr QRDHHX; ticket 722136995952

request_summary: Book using Offer C's ResponseId/selectedOfferId (fresh Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chain) but cellId taken from Offer B's GetSeatMap response (seat 10C token), cellCode=10B (valid on Offer C)

expected: Request is rejected (4xx, exact shape UNKNOWN per §7.9) because the cellID token embeds the originating ResponseId/OfferId and is bound to the offer it was issued for
actual: STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07, 7th confirmed occurrence) - a cellId issued for a different offer was accepted; a real, ticketed booking was created. Behaviour is now more clearly demonstrated than in earlier rounds (where the seat was silently dropped, passengersSelectedSeats:{}): this time the seat was attached and priced, which shows the cellId token is not validated at all and the seat is chosen from cellCode alone.

view_tc.expected_result: Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN - confirm live per §7.9), since cellID embeds the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.

title: Verify window/aisle/extra-legroom/exit-row seat attributes are programmatically derivable from cellCharacteristics for every Seat-category cell
request_summary: One GetSeatMap response (GulfAir/KSA, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01, 1 ADT) - all 178 Seat cells read and classified (Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chain executed first)
response_summary: 200 - 30 rows x 7 columns; 178 Seat cells, 30 Aisle cells, 2 NoSeat cells; 805 cellCharacteristics entries, every padisCode = "Unknown"
expected: For codes in the sourced canonical PADIS table, the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text; codes outside the table are logged, not failed
actual: Every Seat cell carries a derivable window/aisle/centre marker in its description text; 0 of 178 contradict their column position (A/F=WINDOW, C/D=AISLE_SEAT, B/E=CENTER_SEAT, left/right side consistent). Extra-legroom (LEG_SPACE_SEAT rows 8, 19, 20), bulkhead (row 8) and exit-row (EXIT_ROW_SEAT rows 18-21, 24 seats) are derivable from the text too. padisCode is "Unknown" for 805/805 characteristics, so the PADIS-code route yields nothing for this supplier - attributes are derivable only from the description text (logged, not failed, per the expected result). Unchanged from Rounds 1-7.
evidence: column/description mismatches: 0 of 178; WINDOW=59 (cols A/F), AISLE_SEAT=60, CENTER_SEAT=59; EXIT_ROW_SEAT=24; padisCode Unknown=805/805

view_tc.preconditions: GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails covering a mix of window/aisle/middle/exit-row seats.
view_tc.steps: GetSeatMap -> for every Seat-category cell, read cellCharacteristics[].padisCode -> classify each cell as window/aisle/extra-legroom/other using the reference table -> spot-check against column position and description text.
view_tc.expected_result: For codes present in the canonical reference table, the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text. Codes outside that table are logged, not failed.

title: Verify overall cellAvailability and per-passenger seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries are independently reported and internally consistent (not required to list every passenger)
spec_ref: SPEC.md §2.7; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §11; User Story AC2
request_summary: GetSeatMap for a fresh 3-passenger offer (2 ADT + 1 CHD, BAH-RUH 2027-07-01) - every cell compared against passengersSeatMapAvailability
response_summary: 200 - 176 Seat cells; each of PAX1/PAX2/PAX3 has a 176-code allow-list; every cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger lists PAX1, PAX2 and PAX3
expected: A passenger listed in a cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger should also have that cellCode in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability allow-list; absence of a passenger is valid, completeness is NOT asserted; overall and per-passenger availability may legitimately differ
actual: Internally consistent: 528 passenger-cell price entries (176 x 3), 0 listed for a cell that is absent from that passenger's allow-list, and 0 allow-list codes without a priced cell. GulfAir lists all three passengers on every cell (so the "absence is valid" branch could not be exercised here - fine, it is not required), and the per-passenger paxCellAvailability equals the overall cellAvailability everywhere (0 differences; both AvailablePaid). Note for context: the CHD passenger is offered every exit-row cell (24/24), consistent with the already-tracked BUG-09.
evidence: cells=176; listed-pax-set [PAX1,PAX2,PAX3]=176 cells; listed-but-not-in-allow-list=0; allow-list-but-not-priced=0; paxCellAvailability != cellAvailability: 0; CHD PAX3 present on 24/24 EXIT_ROW_SEAT cells

view_tc.expected_result: Structural consistency only: a passenger listed for a cell should have that cellCode in their own allow-list. Do not assert every passenger appears per cell or that overall and per-passenger availability are equal.

title: Exploratory - confirm GetSeatMap reflects real-time supplier inventory rather than a cached snapshot
request_summary: GetSeatMap #1 (Offer B, seat 10C AvailablePaid) -> Book seat 10C on Offer B -> GetSeatMap #2 with the same Offer B IDs -> GetSeatMap #3 on a fresh Offer C
response_summary: Call #1: 10C = AvailablePaid (178 seat cells). After the Book: call #2 and call #3 both return 10C as NoSeat with cellDetails null (177 seat cells) and 10C absent from the passenger allow-list
expected: UNKNOWN - if reliably forceable, the cell's availability transitions between the calls, confirming a live supplier round-trip rather than a cached response
actual: CONFIRMED live inventory. Previously BLOCKED in every round (no second session), but a single tester can force it: booking a seat on one offer immediately changes the seat map returned for BOTH the same offer and an unrelated fresh offer on the same flight. title: Apply the three universal caller-facing security checks (invalid x-api-key, invalid Client-Id, cross-tenant supplier/credentialsSelector) to GetSeatMap
request_summary: GetSeatMap with a valid KSA-issued offer: (1) invalid x-api-key, (2) invalid Client-Id, (3a) supplier/selector switched to TravelportNdc/UAE, (3b) same supplier GulfAir with credentialsSelector switched to UAE; extra probes: empty x-api-key, bogus selector, omitted selector
response_summary: (1) 401 AuthenticationError; (2) 401 AuthenticationError; (3a) 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "Failed to deserialize the selected offer"; (3b) 200 - the full seat map was returned; extras: empty key 401, bogus selector 400, omitted selector 400
expected: All three variants rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN; reuse the envelope other endpoints produce)
actual: Two of the three checks pass cleanly, but the third only half-passes. Switching to a different SUPPLIER is rejected (400), yet switching only the credentialsSelector to another VALID one for the same supplier (GulfAir/UAE - confirmed valid: it also serves Search with 200) is NOT rejected: GetSeatMap returns the complete seat map for an offer that was created under KSA. So credentialsSelector is not enforced as an authorization boundary on GetSeatMap, contradicting SPEC.md §7.14's description of supplier/credentialsSelector as the API's implicit authorization boundary. Note also that the cross-supplier rejection changed shape vs. earlier rounds (was 409 OperationNotSupported "TravelportNdc does not exists", now 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001) - still a rejection.

summary: Book accepts a cellId issued for a different offer's GetSeatMap response and creates a ticketed booking with the seat attached
expected_value: 4xx validation error rejecting the cellId as not belonging to this offer (no PNR created)
impact: The cellId token is not validated at all, so seat selection is driven purely by cellCode: a caller can submit any stale, foreign or forged token and still be charged and ticketed for the seat. It also defeats the token's only purpose (binding a seat choice to a live offer/passenger).
evidence: Book on Offer C with Offer B's cellId -> 200, pnr QPOJIW, ticket 722136996068, seat 10B attached (60.00 SAR)

summary: GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector)
expected_value: 4xx rejection (offer not found / not authorized for this credentialsSelector), as happens when the supplier is switched
impact: credentialsSelector is the API's per-tenant boundary (SPEC.md §7.14). A caller holding an offerId/responseId from one tenant (KSA) can read that offer's seat map through another tenant's selector (UAE), so cross-tenant isolation depends solely on offer IDs being unguessable. The same gap is likely present on the other offer-consuming endpoints (Book, GetAncillary, FareCheck) - not tested here.
evidence: Offer created under GulfAir/KSA; GetSeatMap sent with GulfAir/UAE -> 200 with the full seat map (~305 KB); supplier switched to TravelportNdc/UAE -> 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; GulfAir/UAE Search -> 200 (UAE is a real GulfAir tenant)
